subject.title: refactor(protocol): pre-publish cheat-window cleanup and vintage tracking

question: Should OpenClaw accept these breaking question, worker, and session-catalog protocol changes as part of the pre-publication compatibility window, based on a confirmed shipped-consumer audit?
rationale: The branch deliberately changes public and plugin-facing protocol shapes; tests can validate consistency but cannot establish the repository's release and external-consumer compatibility policy.

options.title: Approve the compatibility window
options.body: Confirm the shipped-consumer audit and accept the documented beta-only breakage, then require runtime proof and CI-baseline proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve or migrate the old shapes
options.body: Require additive aliases or a documented migration path for any protocol family that has released or external consumers.

options.title: Split the publication cleanup
options.body: Land non-breaking export and metadata cleanup separately, then decide each wire-contract break with narrower compatibility evidence.

recommendation.title: Approve the compatibility window
recommendation.body: Confirm the shipped-consumer audit and accept the documented beta-only breakage, then require runtime proof and CI-baseline proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch history shows the strongest direct connection to the affected protocol and runtime surfaces.
